# 2025 Annual Budget Review

## Summary
This year felt calmer than last. My savings rate came out at 27% of take-home pay, up five points, mostly because I stopped letting small purchases drift. I kept the January habit of moving money on the first working day and raised the monthly transfer twice as my confidence grew. Income rose a little after a mid-year salary adjustment. The big lesson from last year, that fixed costs quietly eat the plan, held true again, so I reviewed every standing order in April and cancelled two I had forgotten about.

## Expenses
Rent stayed the largest line and I kept it near a third of income by negotiating the renewal rather than moving. Groceries averaged 460 EUR a month, higher than my 380 EUR ceiling, which I blame on a run of dinner parties and a longer, colder winter. Utilities settled back after the boiler year and were close to 130 EUR a month. The holiday fund finally balanced: I spent 1750 EUR for two weeks in Portugal and stayed inside the envelope. Transport, insurance and subscriptions were all within a few euros of plan. I replaced a laptop in September for 900 EUR, which I had saved for in advance and did not touch the emergency fund.

## Next Year
Next year I want to push the savings rate toward 30% and keep expenses flat. I moved the monthly surplus into a low-cost index fund so the money works a little harder than it does in the current account. Groceries get a realistic 450 EUR ceiling rather than an aspirational one. I will also redo the standing orders each spring so nothing lingers unseen.
